items.title: Beginner Home Fitness
items.summary: Four weeks of short, friendly sessions that build a regular exercise habit.
items.description: Designed for people who are new to exercise or returning after a long break. You train three days a week with simple bodyweight routines, add one light recovery session, and rest on the remaining days. No equipment is needed.
items.weeklySchedule: 3 training days, 1 light recovery day and 3 rest days each week
items.progression: Week 1 keeps sessions short so you can learn the movements. Week 2 introduces new exercises, week 3 adds a third round and a little more time, and week 4 repeats the most complete sessions so you finish confident. Move on only when the exercises feel controlled; it is fine to repeat a week.
items.recovery: Rest days are part of the plan, not a break from it. A relaxed walk or gentle stretching is fine on rest days. Some muscle soreness in the first weeks is common; if it lasts more than a few days or you feel pain, take extra rest and reduce the effort.

weeks.focus: Learn the basic movements with short, easy sessions.
Add variety: legs, core and a mobility session.
Slightly longer workouts with an extra round.
Consolidate: repeat your most complete sessions with confidence.

days.note: Rest. A short walk is a nice optional extra.
Gentle stretching to help you recover.
Plan complete – take a well-earned rest before choosing what comes next.

items.title: Bodyweight Strength Foundations
items.summary: Build all-round strength with push, pull-style, leg and core sessions.
items.description: For people who can already do a few push-ups (or knee push-ups) and bodyweight squats comfortably. Four strength sessions a week alternate between full-body, upper-body, lower-body and core work, with one mobility session to keep you moving well.
items.weeklySchedule: 4 strength sessions, 1 mobility session and 2 rest days each week
items.progression: Weeks 1 and 2 use circuits so you can practise technique under moderate fatigue. Week 3 introduces straight sets with longer rests for more focused strength work. Week 4 keeps that volume steady rather than increasing it again. Use the easier and harder variations to keep every set challenging but controlled.
items.recovery: Keep at least one rest day after each pair of hard sessions, as scheduled. Sleep and regular meals matter as much as the workouts. If a joint feels painful rather than just tired, swap in the easier variation or rest.

weeks.focus: Learn the circuit format and find the right variation for each exercise.
Add a dedicated core session and a fourth strength day.
Straight sets with longer rests for focused strength work.
Hold the volume steady and aim for better technique, not more reps.

days.note: Plan complete. Note which exercises felt easy – those are ready for the harder variation.

items.title: Low-Impact Movement
items.summary: Get your heart rate up and your legs stronger without any jumping.
items.description: Every session in this plan is low impact: no jumping, hopping or running in place. It suits people who prefer to protect their joints, live in flats with neighbours below, or simply want a gentler start. Expect cardio, standing core work and lower-body strength.
items.weeklySchedule: 3–4 low-impact sessions, 1 recovery session and 2–3 rest days each week
items.progression: Week 1 starts with short sessions. Week 2 adds a leg-strength day, week 3 adds a fourth session, and week 4 introduces a longer low-impact endurance workout. Increase intensity by moving a little faster or bending a little deeper – never by adding jumps.
items.recovery: Low impact does not mean no effort, so recovery still matters. Use rest days to walk, stretch or simply rest. If your legs feel heavy for several days, repeat the previous week before moving on.

weeks.focus: Short low-impact sessions to get comfortable moving.
Add a leg-strength day alongside cardio.
Four sessions in the week with a mobility day.
Try a longer endurance session, still without jumping.

days.note: Plan complete. Well done for showing up through all four weeks.

items.title: Mobility & Consistency
items.summary: Short daily movement sessions to feel less stiff and build an everyday habit.
items.description: Five short sessions a week focused on mobility, stretching and movement breaks. Most take under ten minutes, which makes this plan a good fit for busy weeks, long days at a desk, or as a companion to other activities such as walking.
items.weeklySchedule: 5 short mobility or stretching sessions and 2 rest days each week
items.progression: The aim is regularity rather than intensity. Weeks 1 and 2 introduce the routines; weeks 3 and 4 use the longer full-body flow more often. Over time, many people find they can move a little further into each position – let that happen gradually rather than forcing it.
items.recovery: Mobility work should feel pleasant. Breathe slowly, never bounce into a stretch, and back off if you feel pinching or sharp pain. Rest days are still scheduled so the habit stays sustainable.

weeks.focus: Meet the routines: morning, desk, evening, shoulders and hips.
Use the full-body flow more often and add a lower-body stretch.
Keep the rhythm going and notice what feels easier than in week 1.

days.note: Plan complete. Keep the routines you enjoyed most in your week.
